material_updates.scope: Actual real/circular O(d) pure ensembles give full-domain absolute-spectrum majorants on this class. They do not make general spectral positive-part rounding a physical channel.

An exact C5 frame defeats every scalar allocation of an optimal L+G envelope, but a more flexible local-dual gluing certificate provesC2 for the same frame. This is a failed proof ansatz, not a legal C2 counterexample.

A separately constructed canonical EB comparator dominates the HS spectral positive part using broadcast trees and full-space regression. This bypasses, and does not invalidate, the earlier failed direct spectral-positive-part channel lift or scalar-dual ansatz.

EXACT GENERAL GATE AND PRESERVED FAILED EXTENSIONS
2026-10-09. Universal finite C and sharp C=2 remain UNKNOWN.

ALL-FRAME FORM OF THE EXACT TARGET
Let tau=Tr/d and H_0 be the real traceless Hermitian HS space. For any
positive frame operator Q=sum_i |A_i><A_i| with A_i in H_0, put
  V(Q)=sum_i tau(A_i^2),
  s_Phi(Q)=sum_i tau[A_i Phi(A_i)],
  k(Q)=max_{sum_y p_y pi_y=I/d} sum_y p_y sum_i [Tr(pi_y A_i)]^2,
where pi_y are pure density matrices. Finite ensembles suffice by first-
and second-moment Caratheodory. k(Q) is the exact canonical support; it
does not mean a finite chosen seed hull or a PPT relaxation.

Canonical maps form a compact convex set, and all maps fix I. Cone
separation shows that a ONE-channel full-domain factor C comparator
exists for each Phi exactly when for EVERY positive Q
  V(Q)-k(Q)<=C[V(Q)-s_Phi(Q)].                       (G1)
The optimizing ensemble may depend on Q before separation, but the final
channel cannot depend on the requested observable. CANONICAL_REDUCTION.txt
shows that arbitrary TP EB comparators have the same support for this
full-domain problem. Thus canonical versus arbitrary EB is not the
remaining obstruction.

For the conjecturally sharp C=2, the missing inequality is
  2s_Phi(Q)<=V(Q)+k(Q)                              (G2)
for arbitrary Q and legal Phi. Let R be the normalized Choi state of the
supplied broadcaster, symmetrized on B,C. Then R>=0, Tr R=1, all three
single-register marginals are I/d, and its AB marginal is the Choi state
of an HS-self-adjoint channel. Writing
  W(Q)=sum_i (A_i)^T tensor (A_i^B+A_i^C),
we have Tr[R W(Q)]=2s_Phi(Q). The exact general star obligation is
  max_{R with those legal constraints} Tr[R W(Q)]<=V(Q)+k(Q).       (G3)
This is not an unrestricted operator-norm bound. The fixed tracial
marginals and Choi self-adjointness constraints are part of the target.

WHAT THE CLIFFORD MECHANISM CHANGES
For a Clifford span, all attainable expectation vectors lie in a unit
Euclidean ball; every direction has a reference-preserving spectral
ensemble. Therefore k(Q)=lambda_max(Q), V(Q)=Tr Q. Orthogonal changes of
frame preserve the Clifford relations. The weighted star lemma proves
||W(Q)||<=Tr Q+lambda_max(Q), stronger than (G3), and yields an explicit
single covariance S=(2T-I)_+ with a feasible canonical ensemble. For
arbitrary observable spaces these three facts fail: the expectation body

CANONICAL REDUCTION FOR THE EXACT FULL-DOMAIN DIRICHLET INTERFACE
Independent reconstruction, 2026-10-09. Status: elementary proof supplied;
external correctness/priority not established. No universal constant claimed.

Let H_d be the real Hilbert space of Hermitian d-by-d matrices with
<A,B>_tau=Tr(AB)/d. Let Phi be a unital, trace-preserving channel, with
Phi HS-self-adjoint. Let Lambda be any CPTP entanglement-breaking map,
not initially assumed unital or HS-self-adjoint. Interpret its quadratic
form through S=(Lambda+Lambda*)/2.

Suppose <A,(I-S)A> <= C <A,(I-Phi)A> for every Hermitian A, with C finite.
Put D=C(I-Phi)-(I-S). D is a positive semidefinite real HS operator.
Trace preservation implies Lambda*(I)=I and Tr Lambda(I)=d. Thus
<I,D I>=0. Positivity implies D I=0: for any A the quadratic polynomial
<I+tA,D(I+tA)> has vanishing constant term, so its linear term must vanish.
Since Phi(I)=I, D I=(S-I)I, hence S(I)=I. But
S(I)=(Lambda(I)+Lambda*(I))/2=(Lambda(I)+I)/2.
Therefore Lambda(I)=I. Full-domain form domination forces unitality.

Choose a finite EB representation
Lambda(X)=sum_y Tr(E_y X) sigma_y,
E_y>=0, sum_y E_y=I, sigma_y>=0, Tr sigma_y=1.
Discard E_y=0. Write p_y=Tr E_y/d and rho_y=E_y/(d p_y). Then
sum_y p_y rho_y=I/d, and unitality implies sum_y p_y sigma_y=I/d.

Use the two reference ensembles, each with half its original weight:
  {(p_y/2,rho_y)} union {(p_y/2,sigma_y)}.
This is a single ensemble with barycenter I/d. It defines one POVM with
effects M_(y,0)=d p_y rho_y/2=E_y/2 and
M_(y,1)=d p_y sigma_y/2. The effects sum to I.
Its canonical EB map is
Psi(X)=(d/2) sum_y p_y[Tr(rho_y X)rho_y+Tr(sigma_y X)sigma_y].
It is CPTP, unital, HS-self-adjoint, and positive as a real HS operator.
For all Hermitian A,
  <A,(Psi-S)A>_tau
     = (1/2) sum_y p_y[Tr(rho_y A)-Tr(sigma_y A)]^2 >=0.
Thus I-Psi <= I-S <= C(I-Phi).

Consequences:
1. Existence of any CPTP EB comparator is equivalent to existence of a
   canonical comparator for this exact full-domain inequality, with the
   SAME C. If Lambda was already self-adjoint, S=Lambda.
2. Mixed ensemble states may be refined to pure states. For any mixed
   rho=sum_j q_j pi_j, scalar Jensen gives
   sum_j q_j Tr(pi_j A)^2 >= Tr(rho A)^2 simultaneously for every A.
   Refinement preserves the barycenter and further improves Psi's form.
3. Failure against the unrestricted canonical POVM cone DOES refute
